title: Partial<T>
definition: A built-in utility type that constructs a new type where all properties of the given Type `T` are set to optional.
simpleExplanation: Imagine an application form with 20 required fields. `Partial` takes a photocopy of that form, crosses out the word 'Required' next to every single field, and writes 'Optional'.
realWorldExample: Updating a user profile via a PATCH request. You don't want to send the entire `User` object (with ID, email, password) just to update their username. You type the payload as `Partial<User>`.

basic: What does `Partial` do to required properties?
intermediate: Does `Partial` make deeply nested properties optional?

answers.question: Does it make deeply nested properties optional?
answers.answer: No! `Partial` is shallow. It only makes the top-level keys optional. If your object has `{ config: { theme: string } }`, `config` becomes optional, but if you DO provide `config`, you MUST provide `theme`. Deep partials require a custom recursive mapped type.
